hints.title: Use the information about the first equation
hints.body: Sketch y=cosx only on the stated open interval. Move a horizontal line through the graph and identify which nonzero heights give the required number of intersections.
hints.recap: The given root count restricts the horizontal level.
hints.pitfall: Check peaks, troughs and excluded endpoints separately.
hints.pause: Determine the possible values of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> from the first equation.

recall.reminder: The given root count restricts the horizontal level.

hints.title: Keep both signs and change the interval
hints.body: Two real numbers have equal squares when they are equal or opposite. Apply this to cos2x and c, then use u=2x and convert both ends of the interval.
hints.recap: A squared trigonometric equation can involve two distinct horizontal levels.
hints.pitfall: Counting on the original interval after changing the angle misses roots.
hints.pause: Write the two cosine equations and the open interval for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: A squared trigonometric equation can involve two distinct horizontal levels.

hints.title: Count on monotonic pieces
hints.body: Mark the turning points of cosine on your new interval. Count intersections with each permitted level on those pieces, checking whether any intersection is repeated.
hints.recap: Separate branches and endpoint checks make the count reliable.
hints.pitfall: A turning-point intersection belongs to the graph only once.
hints.pause: Combine the two disjoint counts and choose the corresponding total.

recall.reminder: Separate branches and endpoint checks make the count reliable.

solution:
On 0<x<3π/2, the equation cosx=c has two solutions exactly when −1<c<0. Positive levels meet only the first decreasing part, c=−1 meets the trough once, and c=0 is excluded by the question.

The new equation is equivalent to cos2x=c or cos2x=−c. Let u=2x, so 0<u<3π. Both levels are strictly between −1 and 1 and are distinct.

On each of (0,π), (π,2π) and (2π,3π), cosine meets each level exactly once. Thus each equation supplies three solutions, with no overlap, giving six in total. Answer D.
knowledgePattern: Count both cosine levels after squaring and rescaling an open interval
